review_candidates.title: Azure DevOps Engineer
review_candidates.description: Job Summary In this role you will design and run our Azure DevOps pipelines, write and maintain the Terraform that defines our Azure estate, and set the standards for how Azure resources are sized, secured, tagged and paid for. You will work alongside our network, security and Microsoft 365 engineers, and you will be the person they come to when something needs to be automated, repeatable and reviewable. About Rozmith Rozmith is a security-first managed IT and cybersecurity partner for insurance, financial services and other regulated firms across the US, UK and Europe. We run our clients' IT and security day to day and handle the IT side of their mergers and acquisitions, with teams in Atlanta, London and Skopje. What You'll Do Azure DevOps platform and pipelines Design, build and maintain multi-stage YAML pipelines in Azure DevOps for infrastructure and application delivery. Own the Azure DevOps organization: projects, repos, branch policies, service connections, agent pools, environments and approval gates. Run self-hosted and Microsoft-hosted build agents, including scale-set agents, and keep them patched and right-sized. Build reusable pipeline templates so new projects start from a reviewed, standard pattern. Integrate Azure Boards, Repos, Pipelines and Artifacts into one traceable flow from work item to deployment. Support the Rozmith PSA build (our in-house service platform): environments, release pipelines and its Jira integration. Infrastructure as code with Terraform Write, review and maintain Terraform for Azure using the AzureRM, AzAPI and AzureAD providers. Build and version a library of reusable Terraform modules for common patterns: hub-and-spoke networking, landing zones, AKS, App Service, Key Vault, storage and private endpoints. Manage Terraform state securely in Azure Storage with locking, encryption and least-privilege access. Run plan-and-apply through pipelines with peer review, policy checks and manual approval for production. Detect and resolve configuration drift; import existing click-built resources into code. Azure resource architecture and governance Apply the Azure Well-Architected Framework and Cloud Adoption Framework when choosing and sizing services. Define and enforce management group, subscription and resource group structure, naming and tagging standards. Implement Azure Policy, RBAC and Privileged Identity Management so access and configuration meet least-privilege and audit requirements. Choose the right service for each workload: PaaS over IaaS where it fits, reserved capacity and savings plans where usage is steady. Track and reduce spend with Cost Management budgets, alerts, rightsizing and cleanup of orphaned resources. Security, reliability and operations Use managed identities and workload identity federation in place of stored secrets; keep the rest in Key Vault. Build secret scanning, dependency scanning and IaC scanning into pipelines, and fix what they find. Feed pipeline and cloud findings into Defender for Cloud, Tenable and Axonius so they are tracked with the rest of the estate. Set up monitoring and alerting with Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and Application Insights; define SLOs for the services you run. Own backup, disaster recovery and recovery testing for Azure workloads. Lead and write blameless postmortems for incidents in the environments you own. Change control and documentation Deliver changes through our change-control process, with evidence suitable for client audits and regulatory reviews. Write and maintain runbooks, architecture diagrams and standard operating procedures. Mentor engineers on pipelines and Terraform, and review their pull requests. What We're Looking For 4–5 years running a production DevOps environment, with at least 3 of those years primarily in Azure. Hands-on ownership of an Azure DevOps organization: YAML pipelines, templates, service connections, agent pools, environments and approvals. 3+ years writing production Terraform for Azure, including custom modules, remote state, workspaces or environment separation, and pipeline-driven plan/apply. Working knowledge of core Azure services and when to use each: VNets and peering, NSGs, private endpoints, Azure Firewall or NVAs, App Service, Functions, AKS, Azure SQL, Storage, Key Vault and Front Door or Application Gateway. Experience designing subscription and resource group structure, RBAC, Azure Policy and tagging for multiple teams or tenants. Practical cost-management experience: budgets, reservations or savings plans, rightsizing and showing the savings. Scripting in PowerShell and Bash; comfortable reading Python. Git fluency: branching strategies, pull-request reviews and resolving merge conflicts. Solid grounding in Microsoft Entra ID: app registrations, service principals, managed identities and Conditional Access as it affects automation. Experience working inside a formal change-control process. Clear written English. You can write a runbook another engineer can follow at 2 a.m. Nice to Have Managed service provider or multi-tenant experience, using Azure Lighthouse or delegated access across client tenants. Regulated environments (insurance, financial services or healthcare) and frameworks such as SOC 2, NY DFS 23 NYCRR 500, GLBA, UK/EU GDPR, NIS2 or DORA. Azure Landing Zone or Cloud Adoption Framework accelerators, deployed and customized through Terraform. Policy-as-code with Azure Policy, OPA/Conftest or Checkov. Containers and Kubernetes in production on AKS, including Helm and GitOps (Flux or Argo CD). GitHub Actions alongside Azure DevOps, or migrating between the two. Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel integration with pipelines and alerting. Hybrid connectivity: site-to-site VPN, ExpressRoute and third-party firewalls such as FortiGate in Azure. Azure Virtual Desktop deployed and managed with Nerdio. Building or securing AI agent and MCP integrations with internal platforms. Certifications (or the ability to earn them within 12 months): Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400); Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104); Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305); HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate Tools You'll Use CI/CD and source control: Azure DevOps (Repos, Pipelines, Boards, Artifacts), Git; Jira and Confluence for cross-team work Infrastructure as code: Terraform (AzureRM, AzAPI, AzureAD providers), Bicep for reading existing templates Cloud platform: Microsoft Azure: compute, networking, PaaS, AKS, storage, data Virtual desktop: Azure Virtual Desktop with Nerdio Identity and access: Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, PIM, Azure RBAC Governance and cost: Azure Policy, management groups, Cost Management, Azure Advisor Security: Key Vault, Microsoft Sentinel, Snyk and pipeline scanning tools Security integrations: Defender for Cloud, Tenable, Axonius, CrowdStrike Falcon Observability: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights, KQL Scripting: PowerShell, Bash, Azure CLI, Python Network edge: FortiGate NVAs in Azure, VPN gateways, Azure Firewall Platforms we build: Rozmith PSA, Claude with MCP integrations across our operations Working Conditions Remote from the United States, the United Kingdom or Europe. You are employed by the Rozmith entity for your location: Rozmith LLC (US), Rozmith UK Ltd (UK) or Rozmith Macedonia (North Macedonia); other European countries by arrangement. Your hours overlap with US Eastern business hours; your exact schedule is set by location. Participates in a shared after-hours rotation. Benefits by location. US: flexible (unlimited) paid time off and Rozmith's benefit plans. UK: statutory annual leave and workplace pension. Europe: statutory leave, benefits and contributions under local law. Company laptop provided, plus paid certification prep, exam vouchers and training. You must be authorized to work in the country you work from. Some client environments require a background check. Your First 180 Days Day 30: Gain access to our Azure DevOps organization and tenants, review existing pipelines and Terraform, and deliver a written assessment of gaps in state management, secrets handling, tagging and cost. Day 90: Ship a standard pipeline template and a first set of versioned Terraform modules; bring at least one client environment fully under code, with plan/apply through pipelines and approvals. Day 180: Make Terraform the default for new Azure work across clients, enforce tagging and policy baselines, report measurable cost savings, and publish runbooks the rest of the team uses without you. Where It Leads Grow into platform architecture, set cloud engineering standards across our clients, or shape the platforms we build for ourselves, including the Rozmith PSA. We advance people on results, not time served.
